articles.title: Libya: UN Special Representative for Children and Armed Conflict Welcomes Amendments to Conscription Laws bringing the age of recruitment to 18 years
articles.description: New York, 16 November 2026 – A milestone for children in Libya who can no longer be recruited or used in the Armed Forces. The adoption on 2 November 2026, by the House of Representatives of the State of Libya, of amendments to Law No. 40 of 1974 on Service in the Armed Forces and Law No. 21 of 1991 on Mobilization, by majority, is welcomed by Under-Secretary-General Vanessa Frazier, the UN Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Children and Armed Conflict. The amendments specifically prohibit the recruitment of persons under the age of 18 years, as well as their involvement, directly or indirectly, in military operations, and establish criminal liability for any person who recruits or uses persons below the prescribed age. The Special Representative further welcomes that a new provision was introduced to the Penal Code to criminalize underage recruitment and establish a penalty of up to ten years’ imprisonment for recruiting children under 18. “I welcome this positive development which testifies to Libya’s commitment to the protection of children, in line with its obligations under the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child and its Optional Protocol on the Involvement of Children in Armed Conflict,” stressed USG Frazier. Previously, the two laws allowed recruitment into the armed forces from the age of 17. These amendments close the legal gap and bring Libya into compliance with its international commitments. The United Nations remains committed to continue supporting Libya in strengthening the protection of children, preventing grave violations and addressing vulnerabilities of children, including the risks of trafficking and exploitation.
